pivotal_trials.design: 26-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with stratified 3:1 randomization
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects at Week 26 with albumin-adjusted serum calcium within normal range AND independence from active vitamin D AND independence from therapeutic doses of calcium (≤600 mg/day) AND no increase in study drug
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 26, 45/61 (74%) of palopegteriparatide subjects met the composite endpoint vs 1/21 (5%) placebo; treatment difference 69.1% (P<0.0001)

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥5%): injection site reactions (39% vs 5% placebo), vasodilatory signs/symptoms (28% vs 0), headache (21% vs 10%), diarrhea (10% vs 5%), back pain (8% vs 0), hypercalcemia (8% vs 0), oropharyngeal pain (7% vs 0). Serious hypercalcemia and hypocalcemia have occurred.
target_moa: Parathyroid hormone analog (PTH(1-34)); PTH(1-34) transiently conjugated to a branched 40 kDa methoxypolyethylene glycol (mPEG) carrier via a TransCon linker, restoring PTH activity to raise serum calcium
modality: peptide (PTH(1-34) analog PEGylated via TransCon linker; drug-device combination product)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held because the application did not raise significant efficacy, safety or other issues requiring input from external experts.

summary.text: Palopegteriparatide (a new molecular entity) received orphan drug designation for hypoparathyroidism in 2018. The original NDA was submitted August 31, 2022 and received a Complete Response on April 28, 2023 for product quality/device deficiencies; the resubmission (November 14, 2023) was reviewed under Priority review and approved. No advisory committee was convened; no accelerated approval.

citations.quote: FDA designated palopegteriparatide as an orphan drug product (DRU-2018-6388) for the treatment of hypoparathyroidism on June 4, 2018.

On August 31, 2022, the Applicant submitted an initial marketing application for palopegteriparatide as “a parathyroid hormone (PTH) analog indicated for [REDACTED]”. On April 28, 2023, FDA issued a Complete Response (CR) due to critical product quality deficiencies and device concerns (refer to the CR Letter in DARRTS dated April 28, 2023, and to Section 3.2 below).
On November 14, 2023, the Applicant submitted a Complete Response.

requirement.text: 4677-1 Perform a lactation study (milk only) in lactating women who have received therapeutic doses of palopegteriparatide using a validated assay to assess concentrations of palopegteriparatide in breast milk and the effects on the breastfed infant.

requirement.text: 4677-2 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to palopegteriparatide during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, and adverse effects on the developing fetus, neonate, and infant. Assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life. The study should also collect adverse event data for lactating women and infants exposed to palopetgeriparatide through breastfeeding to assess for any potential risks to the infant from breastfeeding. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
